messages:
incident-bot: P0 alert for AcmeCorp (dedicated/VPC) - spike in 5xx + websocket disconnects via customer gateway. >300 errors in last 5m, 40% of streaming sessions failing. Paging oncall.
Maria: seeing repeated `proxy_connect_timeout` and nginx 504s from the gateway logs forwarded by Acme. Also connection resets from our streaming frontends to the customer's gateway.
Doug: confirm this is only for their dedicated pool or across tenants?
Maria: looks isolated to AcmeCorp dedicated pool nodes (dedicated-gpu-pool-acme-*). Other tenants normal. CPU/GPU util ~60-70%, not fully saturated.
Sam CS: Acme oncall (Tom) says their app gateway started returning 502/504s around 09:02 UTC after a config push. They rolled back but issues persist. They're on a managed gateway in their VPC.
Beth: getting a lot of CLOSE_WAIT on our streaming proxies to the customer's gateway, and many sessions stuck in ESTABLISHED then drop. Could be their gateway not closing sockets cleanly -> our retries pile up.
Ryan: timeline - root alert 09:05 UTC. We saw first signs at 09:01 UTC. Acme deployed at 08:58 UTC per their CS.
Infra Lead: can we temporarily reduce our retry bursts to them and route streaming to fallback region? Suggest: drop client-side retry from 3 -> 1 for Acme, reduce connection keepalive timeouts to 15s.
Maria: pushed a canary config to streaming-proxies to cut retries for customer route to 1. Monitoring now.
Oncall-SRE: @Infra Lead what about websocket idle_timeouts? nginx default upstream_read_timeout is 60s, if their gateway is slow maybe we should extend upstream_read_timeout instead of and/or lower proxies retries.
Infra Lead: doing both: lowering retries and increasing upstream_read_timeout to 120s for Acme route. Pushing in 30s.
VPC Support Bot: Note: direct peering metrics show ~20% packet retransmit between our egress and their gateway during the window 08:59-09:10 UTC. Possible transient network issue inside customer VPC.
Doug: if network retransmit is high, extending timeouts may help but won't fix gateway behavior. We should ask Acme to check their gateway logs for socket exhaustion and thread pool saturation.
Sam CS: Acme confirms their gateway hit connection limit; they are adding ephemeral workers but want a stopgap on our side.
Maria: mitigation status - after reducing retries and increasing upstream_read_timeout, 5xx rate dropped from 40%->8% over 6m. websocket disconnect rate down ~65%.
Beth: still seeing a slow leak of socket fds on three dedicated nodes. I'll rotate those nodes out of the pool for GC and restart streaming proxy on them.
Oncall-SRE: I'm going to page Platform infra to investigate proxy FD leak; tagging @Doug and @Infra Lead. Also creating follow-up ticket: INC-ACME-1715.
Doug: started node rotation, cordoning nodes acme-node-07/08/09. Restarting proxies now.
Maria: logs during rotation show backlog drain, no new 5xx spike. Good sign.
Sam CS: relaying to Acme: they will increase gateway connection limit and monitor. They've scheduled a full config review with their infra team.
Infra Lead: postmortem action items so far: 1) implement per-tenant retry/circuit-breaker defaults, 2) automated detection + temporary timeout override for customer-gateway issues, 3) investigate proxy FD leak root cause. 4) run dedicated-pool soak test for gateway-like behavior.
VPC Support Bot: FYI, audit shows Acme's dedicated pool uses older TLS termination proxy which may not support our keepalive optimizations. Recommend compatibility note to onboarding docs.
Beth: handoff to night oncall in 20m - I'll update CONN tracking and include mitigation steps in the incident ticket. :thumbsup:
Maria: final numbers at 09:48 UTC - 5xx baseline returned to normal for Acme, websocket stability improved. Will keep monitoring for 12h. If regress, rollback to full circuit-breaker and route to fallback streaming endpoint.
Oncall-SRE: handing over to Night SRE (Ryan). Ryan you're up, brief: reduced retries, timeout increased, rotated nodes, Acme is increasing gateway capacity. Ticket INC-ACME-1715 created. Escalate if errors >5% for more than 10m.
Ryan: ack. I'll watch dashboards and stay on the ticket. Please ping me directly if Acme opens a new support stream. :eyes:
incident-bot: Incident INC-ACME-1715 created. Severity P0 -> downgraded to P1 at 09:48 UTC after mitigations. Channels: #incidents, #eng-oncall, ticket link https://rwinf/tickets/INC-ACME-1715
Maria: adding a post-incident checklist to the ticket (logs, timeline, config diff, customer gateway logs). Thanks team. :thankyou:
